explication: three.js is a browser JavaScript 3D library. An application developer constructs a scene graph, camera, geometry, and material, then asks a renderer to produce frames on a browser canvas. Rendering selects WebGL or WebGPU execution, where node-based shader definitions become programmable stages and cached pipelines. Supporting branches provide asset loading, animation, audio, WebXR, and the interactive editor. The tree and excerpts establish these subsystem boundaries, but do not expose every renderer/backend call, so uncertain internal links are omitted.
